title: Generator convoy stuck at an unregulated junction — March 2026
summary: A generator dispatched to a critical hospital was held 16 minutes at a junction with broken signals and no police, while transit times across the whole corridor kept growing behind it. The dispatch decision had been right; the route was never guaranteed.
outcome: A police unit arrived and the convoy completed the last stretch in 6 minutes. Lesson: key junctions must be regulated before the convoy passes — an unregulated junction can cost more than the entire drive.

title: Police pulled from a junction and the corridor seized up — May 2026
summary: The police unit regulating the busiest junction was diverted to a hospital emergency. Within minutes congestion climbed along every route that crossed the junction, delaying three crews that were already en route elsewhere.
outcome: The unit returned 35 minutes later and the corridor recovered. Lesson: lifting regulation from a junction has a cost that shows up minutes later on every route through it — only divert if the new destination outweighs holding the corridor.

title: Congestion trend detected and regulated before the first convoy — July 2026
summary: As the blackout began, congestion at the junction started climbing minutes before any convoy was dispatched. A police unit was sent on the trend alone and the junction was already being directed when the first generator came through.
outcome: No convoy lost time at the junction for the rest of the crisis. Lesson: send police on the congestion trend, not once crews are already blocked — a junction held in advance is cheaper than one unblocked in a hurry.
